redesign_note: v0_2 was built entirely from SEBI/HO/IMD/DF3/CIR/P/2017/114 (2017) as amended in 2020. The new source corpus contains 'Categorization and Rationalization of Mutual Fund Schemes.pdf', a SEBI circular dated 2026-02-26 (no. HO/24/13/15(2)2026-IMD-RAC4/I/5764/2026) that explicitly SUPERSEDES that basis: Solution Oriented Schemes are discontinued and replaced by a new 'Life Cycle Funds' group, several investment-mandate thresholds changed (e.g. Multi Cap Fund's equity floor moved 65%->75%), several debt categories were renamed, and Section V ('Other Schemes') collapsed from 13 finely-split subtypes down to just 2 broad categories (Index Funds/ETFs; FoFs Overseas/Domestic) at the top level -- with a separate, richer sub-categorization (Annexure C) that applies only to FoFs with multiple underlying funds. Because AMCs have a 6-month compliance window and every dataset in this corpus (the AMFI monthly reports, the scheme-level CSV) predates 2026-02-26, this taxonomy models BOTH regimes explicitly rather than picking one, with an explicit crosswalk between them. This is what actually resolves the graph-underutilization problem flagged in the original AARE baseline report: a query about 'AI disclosure requirements for advisers' now has real clause-level regulatory nodes to traverse, not just corporate-hierarchy edges.

legacy_unclassified.note: 50 raw Scheme_Category strings appear in mutual_fund_data.csv; 8 of them do not map to ANY category name in either the 2017 or 2026 SEBI circulars. They total 6,622 of 16,245 rows (40.8% of the whole CSV) and need explicit handling rather than being silently dropped or force-matched to a real category.

structural_changes_vs_legacy: Solution Oriented Schemes discontinued outright (clause 2.6.3.16) -- existing Retirement/Children's Fund schemes must stop subscriptions and merge into a comparable scheme with SEBI approval.

New 'Life Cycle Funds' group (D): target-date glide-path funds, tenure 5-30 years in 5-year multiples, max 6 concurrently open per AMC, with a full duration-banded equity/debt/gold-silver glide table (Annexure B) and a graduated exit load (3%/2%/1% in years 1/2/3).

Section 'Other Schemes' (E) collapsed from 13 legacy subtypes to 2: 'Index Funds/ETFs' (single category, min. 95% index-tracking, no equity/debt/domestic/international split) and 'FoFs (Overseas/Domestic)' (single category, min. 95% in the underlying fund).

A separate, much richer sub-categorization applies ONLY to FoFs with multiple underlying funds (Annexure C): Equity-oriented FOF Domestic (Diversified / Sectoral-Thematic), Debt-oriented FOF Domestic, Hybrid FOF Domestic (Aggressive/Conservative/Income+Arbitrage/Dynamic/Multi-Asset), Commodity-based FOF Domestic, Overseas FOF (Country- or Region-specific, Equity or Debt), and Domestic+Overseas FOF -- each further split into Active/Passive/Omni sub-options, with per-AMC quota limits.

Multiple equity-category minimum-investment thresholds raised, e.g. Multi Cap Fund's equity floor moved from 65% to 75% of total assets (25/25/25 split across large/mid/small cap now computed on the higher base); Dividend Yield/Value/Contra/Focused/Sectoral/Thematic funds' floors moved from 65% to 80%.

Several debt categories renamed (not just re-thresholded): 'Ultra Short Duration Fund' -> 'Ultra Short Term Fund'; 'Short Duration Fund' -> 'Short Term Fund'; 'Medium Duration Fund' -> 'Medium Term Fund'; 'Medium to Long Duration Fund' -> 'Medium to Long Term Fund'; 'Long Duration Fund' -> 'Long Term Fund'; 'Dynamic Bond Fund' -> 'Dynamic Term Fund'; 'Floater Fund' -> 'Floating Interest Rates Fund'; 'Gilt Fund with 10 Year Constant Duration' -> '10-year Constant Maturity Gilt Fund'.
'Low Duration Fund' (legacy 6-12mo) is absorbed into a renamed 'Ultra Short to Short Term Fund' band, rather than existing as its own category.

NEW debt category: 'Sectoral Fund' (debt) -- min. 80% debt of a specified sector (Financial Services, Energy, Infrastructure, Housing, Real Estate), only in AA+ and above rated corporate bonds. Not present in the legacy regime.

Portfolio-overlap ceilings introduced/tightened for sectoral/thematic equity funds (max 50% overlap with other equity schemes, phased in over 3 years) -- a new compliance dimension with no legacy equivalent.

regime_crosswalk_summary.note: All 13 legacy Section V subtypes collapse into just 2 CURRENT_2026 top-level codes; the lost granularity partially re-emerges for multi-underlying FoFs via fof_multi_underlying_subframework, but single-underlying FoFs and all Index Funds/ETFs genuinely lose their asset-class/geography split at the regulatory-taxonomy level going forward.

known_remaining_gaps: Close-ended scheme categories (Fixed Maturity Plans, Capital Protection Oriented Schemes, Interval Funds) are mentioned structurally in the AMFI monthly reports (Sections B/C) but their specific SEBI investment-mandate definitions are not present in the Categorization circular in this corpus -- only their reported instance counts are available.

The CURRENT_2026 circular's Annexure C multi-underlying FoF sub-framework defines category names, quotas, benchmarks, and naming conventions in detail, but this corpus contains no reported instance data for it yet (too new -- circular is 5 months old as of this corpus's most recent AMFI report).

TER (expense ratio) slabs, exit-load schedules (outside Life Cycle Funds' stated 3/2/1% schedule), and distributor commission structures remain separate SEBI-regulated domains with no source document in this corpus.

6,622 CSV rows (40.8%) carry pre-2017 legacy category labels (Income/Growth/ELSS/Liquid/Gilt/Balanced/Money Market/Assured Return) that map to neither regime cleanly -- see legacy_unclassified. These need either a dedicated LEGACY_PRE_2017 bucket in the graph or a semantic-similarity backfill pass against Scheme_Name text before they can be classified with confidence.
